newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe money rates seen stable to year-end.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe money rates seen stable to year-end.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market will probably stay in their current 20 to 25 percent range into the new year, market analysts said on Wednesday.
"It's very difficult to say but I don't foresee any great changes in the rates by December," one analyst told Reuters.
Money dealers said a current market shortage brought about by limited maturities in short-term securities had seen rates harden by a percentage point or two during the last week.
But analysts said Z$3.6 billion worth of maturities expected in November, and a further Z$9.1 billion in December were likely to add liquidity to the market.
"It looks like the increased liquidity might depress the rates, but on the other hand funds going out of the system towards payments might offset that," said one dealer.
But some analysts said rates were also likely to be directed by inflation. However, they added recent fluctuations made it difficult to pinpoint which direction interest rates were likely to take.
"Inflation figures have been rather volatile of late, we saw it down at 17.7 percent in August then it came up to 20.6 percent in September....there's no clear trend really," a dealer said.
"We should expect to see rates settle down in the first quarter of next year."
An economist with the Commercial Bank of Zimbabwe, Danny Dube, predicted a marginal rise in inflation which was likely to put a slight upward pressure on rates.

"I would expect a slight rise in inflation because the effects of some recent fuel price increases have yet to come through and I believe the 20 percent salary increment government paid to civil servants also still has to make an impact on the market," Dube said.
"But on the other hand, with positive predictions for the coming rainy season, inflationary forces are more likely to be down than up," he told Reuters.

On Wednesday treasury bills were quoted at 19.60 percent while negotiable certicates of deposit (NCDs) were trading at 25.5 percent. Bankers acceptances were at 21,50 percent and call money was quoted at 22 percent.
